## Natural history notes

A medium-sized wading bird characterized by its white plumage, long downcurved orange-red bill, reddish legs, and black wingtips that are most visible in flight. In Florida, it is common in marshes, swamps, mangroves, wet prairies, ponds, mudflats, lawns, and coastal wetlands where shallow water or soft soil provides foraging habitat. It feeds mainly on crayfish, crabs, aquatic insects, small fish, frogs, and other small animals, using its sensitive bill to probe in mud, water, and wet vegetation.
